## Issues

### ISSUE-0001 [Open] Hanf number claim is imprecise/overstated
- **Category:** Supplement/remark error
- **Location:** supplement / 関連する結果 / ハンフ数
- **Detail:** The supplement says that using an indiscernible sequence of type $\omega_{1}$ one obtains a 'refinement' of the fact that a theory with an infinite model has arbitrarily large models. This is imprecise: the Hanf number of first-order logic is $\beth_{\omega_{1}}$ (a large cardinal-like bound), and the standard argument uses an indiscernible sequence of type $\omega_{1}$ together with the EM model to show that if $T$ has a model of size $\beth_{\omega_{1}}$ (or the relevant bound) then it has arbitrarily large models. The statement as written is vague and does not correctly identify what the Hanf-number argument refines.
- **Proposed fix:** The Hanf number of first-order logic is $\beth_{\omega_{1}}$: using an indiscernible sequence of type $\omega_{1}$ and the EM model, one shows that if a theory has a model of size $\beth_{\omega_{1}}$ then it has models of all larger cardinalities. This refines the elementary fact that a theory with an infinite model has arbitrarily large models.
- **Reported:** 2026-10-28 (10fede1)

### ISSUE-0002 [Open] 0-sharp description as 'indiscernibles of L' is imprecise
- **Category:** Supplement/remark error
- **Location:** supplement / 関連する結果 / 集合論との接点
- **Detail:** The supplement states that $0^{\sharp}$ is 'the class of indiscernible elements of the constructible universe $\mathbf{L}$'. This is imprecise: $0^{\sharp}$ is (coded by) the theory of the class of Silver indiscernibles for $\mathbf{L}$, i.e. an Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski type / set of formulas, not literally 'the class of indiscernibles' itself. The indiscernibles are the Silver indiscernibles $I$; $0^{\sharp}$ is the EM set generated by them.
- **Proposed fix:** $0^{\sharp}$ is the Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski set (the theory of the Silver indiscernibles) associated with the class $I$ of Silver indiscernibles for $\mathbf{L}$; it is not the class $I$ itself but the EM type it generates.
- **Reported:** 2026-10-28 (10fede1)

### ISSUE-0003 [Open] Functoriality requires embeddings, not just order embeddings, to preserve EM type
- **Category:** Supplement/remark error
- **Location:** supplement / 高い視点から：添字から構造への関手
- **Detail:** The supplement says that fixing an EM type, an order embedding $I\to J$ is sent to an elementary embedding $\mathcal{M}(I)\to\mathcal{M}(J)$, giving a functor. This is correct only when the EM type is fixed and the models are built as Skolem hulls of the indiscernibles with that type; but the statement as written omits that the EM type must be held fixed and that the map on models is induced by the term structure. More importantly, the claim that 'order automorphisms become model automorphisms is a special case of functoriality' is fine, but the functor claim needs the hypothesis that the EM type is realized by indiscernibles in both models. As stated it is essentially correct but slightly overstated; the main genuine issue is that the functor is only defined on the category of linear orders with order embeddings and requires the fixed EM type.
- **Proposed fix:** Fix an EM type $\Phi$. Then $I\mapsto\mathcal{M}(I)=\mathrm{Hull}(\{a_{i}:i\in I\})$ with $(a_{i})$ indiscernible of type $\Phi$ is functorial: an order embedding $f\colon I\to J$ induces an elementary embedding $\mathcal{M}(I)\to\mathcal{M}(J)$ sending $a_{i}\mapsto a_{f(i)}$. Order automorphisms give model automorphisms as the special case $I=J$.
- **Reported:** 2026-10-28 (10fede1)
